Suppose you will roll a fair, six-sided die `until you get a 4`. What is the `expected value of the highest number` you roll through this process?


::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💡 Hint

Because you know you will eventually see a 4, the possible highest numbers are 4, 5 and 6. Suppose k 
k is the highest and compute $\mathbb{P}(Max = k)$
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💡 Solution

Since 4, 5 and 6 can be the first in the sequence with equal probability we have $\mathbb{P}(k = 4) = 1/3.$ Then, the maximum is 6 if you see 6 before 4, again, since each number has the same probability to be seen first, we have $\mathbb{P}(k = 6) = 1/2.$ Finally, the maximum is 5 only if 5 is seen before 4 and the 4 is seen before the 6 so $\mathbb{P}(k = 5) = 1/6.$

Thus, $\boxed{\mathbb{E}(k)=4/3 + 6/2 + 5/6 = \frac{31}{6}.}$
:::
